text:
Lake Champlain has a Lake Wind Advisory today, with southeast winds building to 15 to 25 knots and waves reaching 4 to 6 feet. If you’re headed out, go early and be off the water before this afternoon’s rough-up. Around Burlington, it’s a wet one, with showers and thunderstorms, a high near 59, and a real chance of heavy rain. The front is stalling over us, so this isn’t a quick passing shower, expect roughly three-quarters to an inch of rain today and tonight, with gusty south winds adding to the chill.

Wednesday is an improvement, but not a clean break. Showers should taper before late morning, then it stays mostly cloudy with a high near 60, though the forecast spread is wide on how wet and warm the day gets. I’d keep the rain jacket handy. Another strong, windy rainmaker arrives Friday, followed by a much colder, blustery weekend with scattered snow showers. Plan on indoor time today, and wait until Wednesday afternoon for a better walk.

A rainy, blustery day near 56, with showers lingering and winds turning fierce overnight.

Mostly sunny and milder Monday, near 57, with a south wind making it feel breezier.
